version.changelog: Updated the ClawHub clipboard-memory skill package to 1.3.2 so the revised command and setup-check references can publish cleanly

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clipboard-memory
Version: 1.3.2

The skill bundle provides a well-documented interface for an AI agent to interact with 'clipmem', a local clipboard history utility for macOS. The instructions in SKILL.md are clearly aligned with the stated purpose of recalling user-copied data, and the diagnostic script (scripts/check-setup.sh) is robustly implemented with no signs of malicious intent or data exfiltration. While the skill accesses sensitive clipboard history, this is its explicit and intended function, and the documentation emphasizes local, privacy-preserving storage.

llm.summary: This skill is internally consistent: it queries a local macOS clipboard archive via the clipmem CLI, asks only for the binary (installable via Homebrew or cargo), and its instructions match the declared purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the behavior: the skill only requires the clipmem binary and operates on the local clipmem SQLite archive (~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3). Nothing requested (no env vars, no external credentials, no unrelated binaries) appears out of scope for recalling clipboard history.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to run clipmem subcommands (recall, timeline, search, get, export, doctor, service status) and to run the included setup-check script. All referenced files/paths (database path, scripts) and commands are relevant to clipboard retrieval. The skill does read local clipboard DB metadata and can export raw bytes to disk or restore items to the clipboard — this is expected for its purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install spec is a Homebrew formula (clipmem) from the tap tristanmanchester/tap and a cargo option. Homebrew installs are normal, but the tap is third-party (not core/homebrew); users may want to verify the tap/author before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, no credentials, and no unrelated config paths are requested. The skill's access is limited to the clipmem binary and its local DB, which matches the described functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated or cross-skill privileges. It relies on clipmem's background watcher/LaunchAgent for capture, which is normal for a clipboard archival tool. It does not modify other skills' configurations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill reads the local clipmem archive (your macOS clipboard history) and can export raw bytes to disk or restore items to the clipboard — so it can access anything you copied, including secrets. Before installing: (1) confirm you trust the clipmem source (the Homebrew tap tristanmanchester/tap or the cargo package author); (2) be aware enabling the background watcher (clipmem setup or brew services start clipmem) will persist clipboard history to ~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3; (3) review and remove the skill if you no longer want clipboard history accessible. If you have highly sensitive data concerns, avoid installing or disable collection via clipmem settings/LaunchAgent.
